headline: Polish security services meet after 'serious' threat to PM and defense minister

Polish security services meet after 'serious' threat to PM, defense minister

 FILE PHOTO: EU Council President Donald Tusk holds British Prime Minister Theresa May's Brexit letter which was delivered by Britain's permanent representative to the European Union Tim Barrow (not pictured) that gives notice of the UK's intention to leave the bloc under Article 50 of the EU's Lisbon Treaty in Brussels, Belgium, March 29, 2017. 
 Yves Herman | Reuters
 Polish security services convened a special meeting on Sunday after receiving information about a potential attack on Prime Minister Donald Tusk and Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz, a spokesperson said.
 Special services spokesperson Jacek Dobrzynski said he could not go into details but authorities were treating the threat as "deadly serious".
 "We are talking about a high probability of these threats being carried out," he told reporters.
 Interior Ministry Spokesperson Karolina Galecka said an email with information about the potential attack had been forwarded to police by the State Protection Service, which is responsible for ministers' security.
 While violent crime is relatively rare in Poland, the country is deeply polarised politically and has faced security threats due to its proximity to the war in Ukraine.
 In August, police detained a 23-year-old man accused of calling for the assassination of senior Polish politicians.
 In 2024, Tusk said he received threats after an assassination attempt on Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico.
